easy.explanation: Jehoahaz the son of Jehu began to reign over Israel in Samaria.
easy.q: Who began to reign over Israel in Samaria?

answers: The sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat
The sins of the kings of Judah
easy.explanation: Jehoahaz followed the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

answers: The hand of Hazael and Ben-hadad, kings of Syria
easy.explanation: The LORD delivered Israel into the hand of the kings of Syria.
easy.q: Into whose hand did the LORD deliver Israel?

answers: Because the king of Syria oppressed Israel
Because he wanted to reign in Judah
medium.explanation: Jehoahaz sought the LORD because the king of Syria oppressed Israel.
medium.q: Why did Jehoahaz besought the LORD?

answers: The LORD gave Israel a saviour and they went out from under Syria
medium.explanation: The LORD gave Israel a saviour, but the people did not depart from their sins.
medium.q: What was the result of Jehoahaz’s prayer?

medium.explanation: The saviour brought Israel deliverance from the Syrians.
medium.q: What does “a saviour” mean in this passage?

answers: The oppression continued without any change
There was relief from oppression, but not complete spiritual repentance
challenge.explanation: Israel went out from under Syria, but did not depart from its sins.
challenge.q: What is shown by Israel receiving deliverance while continuing in Jeroboam’s sins?

answers: Israel had no army at all
challenge.explanation: Only fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen remained.
challenge.q: What do the numbers reveal about Israel’s army?

answers: It had been destroyed and made like dust by threshing
challenge.explanation: The king of Syria had destroyed Israel’s army and made it like dust by threshing.
challenge.q: How is Israel’s military condition described?

paragraphs.title: The Reign of Joash and the Continuation of Israel’s Sins

easy.explanation: Joash his son reigned in the stead of Jehoahaz.

answers: He did that which was good
He did that which was evil
easy.explanation: Joash did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD.
easy.q: What did Joash do in the sight of the LORD?

easy.explanation: Joash fought against Amaziah king of Judah.

answers: He continued in Jeroboam’s sinful way
He went to reign in Judah
medium.explanation: Joash continued in the sinful way established by Jeroboam.
medium.q: What does it mean that Joash departed not from the sins of Jeroboam?

answers: Joash died, then reigned, and fought Amaziah beforehand
Joash reigned, fought Amaziah, and afterward died
Joash reigned, died, and then fought Amaziah
medium.explanation: Joash reigned, fought Amaziah, and then died.
medium.q: What was the correct order of events?
Who sat upon Joash’s throne after his death?

answers: Both did evil and continued in Jeroboam’s sins
challenge.explanation: Both kings did evil and continued in the sins of Jeroboam.
challenge.q: What was similar about the reigns of Jehoahaz and Joash?

answers: His fight against Amaziah king of Judah
His being the son of Jehu
challenge.explanation: Joash is specifically remembered for fighting Amaziah king of Judah.
challenge.q: Which detail distinguishes the account of Joash from that of Jehoahaz?

answers: The royal line continued within Israel’s ruling family
challenge.explanation: Jeroboam sat upon Joash’s throne, showing that the Israelite monarchy continued.
challenge.q: What can be understood from Jeroboam succeeding Joash?

paragraphs.title: Elisha’s Prophecy of Deliverance from Aram

easy.explanation: Joash the king of Israel came down unto Elisha.
easy.q: Who came down to Elisha when he was sick?

easy.explanation: Elisha told Joash to take a bow and arrows.
easy.q: What did Elisha and Joash use in the symbolic act?

easy.explanation: Elisha commanded Joash to open the window eastward.
easy.q: In which direction was the window opened?

answers: The LORD’s deliverance and victory over Syria
medium.explanation: Elisha called it the arrow of the LORD’s deliverance and deliverance from Syria.
medium.q: What did the arrow shot through the window represent?

answers: He smote three times and stopped
medium.explanation: Joash smote three times and stayed.
medium.q: What did Joash do when Elisha told him to smite upon the ground?

answers: Because he did not take the bow
Because he opened the wrong window
Because he did not smite more times
medium.explanation: Elisha said he should have smitten five or six times.
medium.q: Why was the man of God wroth with Joash?

answers: The blows represented the number of victories over Syria
The blows determined Joash’s years of reign
challenge.explanation: Elisha connected Joash’s symbolic blows with the number of times he would smite Syria.
challenge.q: What was the connection between the number of blows and the war’s result?

answers: Joash obeyed, but not with the fullest possible determination
challenge.explanation: Joash obeyed the command, but stopped after only three blows instead of five or six.
challenge.q: What does Elisha’s rebuke suggest about Joash’s three blows?

answers: A sign of rescue and victory in war
challenge.explanation: The arrow represented the LORD’s deliverance of Israel from Syria.
challenge.q: What does “the arrow of deliverance” mean in this prophecy?

paragraphs.title: Elisha’s Death and the Miracle of the Bones

easy.explanation: Elisha died, and they buried him.
Bands of the Moabites invaded the land.
easy.q: Who invaded the land after Elisha’s death?

answers: He revived and stood upon his feet
easy.explanation: When the man touched Elisha’s bones, he revived and stood upon his feet.
easy.q: What happened to the man who touched Elisha’s bones?

answers: The buriers saw a band of men and hurried
They wanted to bury him beside the king
Elisha commanded them to do it
medium.explanation: The buriers saw the Moabite band and cast the man into the sepulchre.
medium.q: Why was the man cast into Elisha’s sepulchre?

answers: The man revived, touched the bones, and was then cast into the sepulchre
The man was cast into the sepulchre, touched the bones, and revived
Elisha rose, and then the man was buried
medium.explanation: The man was cast into the sepulchre, touched Elisha’s bones, and revived.
medium.q: What was the correct order of events?

answers: A group of soldiers or raiders
medium.explanation: The bands of the Moabites were groups of raiders invading the land.
medium.q: What is a “band” in this passage?

answers: His influence ended immediately at his death
His connection with a miracle continued after his death
He had been king over Moab
challenge.explanation: Even after Elisha’s death, contact with his bones brought the man back to life.
challenge.q: What does the miracle of the bones emphasize about Elisha?

answers: They were responding to immediate danger
challenge.explanation: They saw the invading band and acted quickly because of the danger.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the buriers’ haste?

answers: Both involve burial, and the burial becomes the setting for a miracle
Elisha’s death caused Moab to become a kingdom
challenge.explanation: The miracle takes place in Elisha’s sepulchre immediately after his death and burial are described.
challenge.q: What connection exists between Elisha’s death and the event that follows?

paragraphs.title: The LORD’s Mercy and the Restoration of Israel’s Cities

easy.explanation: Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.
easy.q: Who oppressed Israel in the days of Jehoahaz?

answers: For the sake of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
For the sake of the Moabite bands
easy.explanation: The LORD had compassion because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
easy.q: For whose sake did the LORD have compassion on Israel?
How many times did Joash beat Ben-hadad?

answers: He took back the cities from Ben-hadad
He restored Hazael to the throne
medium.explanation: Joash took from Ben-hadad the cities that Syria had taken from Israel.
medium.q: What did Joash do after Hazael died?

answers: Joash smote Syria three times as Elisha had said
Joash did not fulfill Elisha’s prophecy
medium.explanation: Elisha had said that Joash would smite Syria three times.
medium.q: What was the connection between Elisha’s prophecy and Joash’s actions?

answers: The LORD would not annihilate Israel
The LORD wanted to make them kings
The LORD sent them into Syria
medium.explanation: The LORD showed mercy and did not destroy Israel.
medium.q: What does “would not destroy them” mean in this passage?

answers: Because of the LORD’s covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
challenge.explanation: The passage directly attributes the LORD’s compassion to his covenant with the patriarchs.
challenge.q: According to the passage, why did the LORD show mercy to Israel?

answers: He attempted to recover the territory lost during his father’s reign
He conquered cities belonging only to Judah
challenge.explanation: Joash recovered cities that Ben-hadad had taken from Jehoahaz his father.
challenge.q: What can be understood from Joash restoring the cities taken from Jehoahaz?

answers: Israel’s cities were restored after three victories over Syria
Hazael died without any change in Israel
challenge.explanation: Joash defeated Ben-hadad three times and recovered the cities of Israel.
challenge.q: How does this section conclude the events of the chapter?
